title: Lettre Tate (mai 66) (Cristaux) : lettre (1966), tapuscrit (s.d.), notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page continues Chapter 2 ('La cohomologie de De Rham est un cristal') of Grothendieck's May 1966 letter to Tate. It lists evidence that the relative de Rham cohomology of a smooth proper f: X -> S should form a crystal on S.

(b) Gauss-Manin. For f smooth, Grothendieck says he has built a canonical absolute connection on Rf_*(Omega^._{X/S}), viewed as an object of D(O_S). This is a connection relative to the absolute base, not only to S. He has not checked that its curvature vanishes, i.e. integrability. He knows integrability only transcendentally: when S is smooth over a reduced base of characteristic 0, comparison with the local system R^q f^an_* C gives it.

In a bracket he warns that one cannot hope the connection always comes from a stratification. In his language a stratification is a crystal structure on the infinitesimal site. He says this fails in characteristic p > 0 because de Rham cohomology of non-complete (e.g. affine) varieties is far too big. In char p, H^0_dR(A^1) = k[x^p] is infinite-dimensional. Hence f must be assumed proper.

(c) He recalls a problem from his 'papier bleu', 'On the de Rham cohomology of algebraic varieties' (Publ. IHES 29, 1966). Take S smooth over C and f: X -> S smooth and proper. The topological Leray spectral sequence H^p(S^an, R^q f^an_* C) => H^*(X^an, C) has an algebraic E_2 term and an algebraic abutment. The E_2 term is de Rham cohomology of S with coefficients in R^q f_*(Omega^._{X/S}) with its integrable Gauss-Manin connection. The abutment is H_dR(X). He asks for a purely algebraic construction of the whole spectral sequence.

2.2. He sets out the precise conjecture in the optimistic case where no isogeny is needed. Crystals of modules on S form an abelian category, so one takes its derived category, whose objects are 'complexes of crystals'. Each such object induces, on every target T of an object (U -> T) of the crystalline site, an ordinary complex in D(O_T). The next page then demands a perfect complex of absolute crystals DR(f) with the following properties: compatible with base change, contravariantly functorial, satisfying Künneth, self-dual with values in the Tate crystal T^d[2d], and with DR(f)(S) = Rf_*(Omega^._{X/S}).

The problem served is to build a crystalline (p-adic, integral) Weil cohomology. It should extend Washnitzer-Monsky and specialise to de Rham cohomology over any lift.
errors: The bracketed argument diagnoses the char-p obstruction only partly. Even for f proper and smooth in characteristic p, the Gauss-Manin connection usually does NOT come from a stratification in the infinitesimal (non-PD) sense. Its p-curvature is nilpotent but in general nonzero (Katz, 1970), for example for the Legendre family of elliptic curves. So properness alone does not rescue the infinitesimal-stratification statement. The correct fix, which Grothendieck himself sketched in the 1966 IHES lectures and Berthelot carried out, is divided-power (PD) stratifications/crystals.

Conversely, for PD-crystals non-properness is not an obstruction to crystal-ness. Berthelot's base change theorem gives a quasi-coherent crystal for smooth quasi-compact f. Properness is needed for finiteness/perfectness, not for the crystal property. 'Too big' (non-finite) and 'not a stratification' are conflated in the bracket.
Integrability of Gauss-Manin was left unverified algebraically. It was later proved algebraically by Katz-Oda (1968); this is a gap, not an error.

deep.surprise_reason: This is the well-known 1966 letter to Tate that founded crystalline cohomology; Berthelot's book cites it. Every idea on the page (Gauss-Manin, the algebraic Leray spectral sequence problem, derived crystals) was taken up and credited. The only point of interest is the slightly mistaken char-p reasoning, which predates PD structures and p-curvature.
transcription_corrections: Line 2-3: 'nullité de la cour-' is completed in hand at the line break; the struck typed word looks like 'torsion' overwritten, but the intended word is 'courbure'.
'sur R réduit de caractéristique nulle': the comma after 'lisse' is a handwritten insertion.
In (c), 'si R est le spectre' has the R typed over another letter; meaning R = Spec C.
The superscript on H in the spectral sequence is 'p' (overtyped).
